chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about wine in which something is made until it ferments. He said: If that which is made in it is the dominant factor over what was made, then there is no harm. This report is rejected on the apparent level by consensus, because there is no disagreement that that in which wine falls becomes impure, and if it becomes impure, its use is not permissible even if it is dominant over it, and that which reveals what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wine if an ingredient is added to it until it ferments or changes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights a key juristic debate regarding *naskh al-ism* (change of name) versus *naskh al-hukm* (change of ruling) when wine is mixed with other substances. While the Imam suggests that if the added ingredient becomes dominant, there is no harm, the report is ultimately rejected by consensus (*ijma'*) because wine inherently causes impurity (*najasah*), rendering it unusable regardless of the dominant substance's presence. This underscores the Shia principle that the fundamental impurity of wine precludes its purification through mere alteration of state or dominance of another element.
